assertions.title: SIGTERM stops accepting new connections
assertions.command_run: Start loom on port 8094; kill -TERM <pid>; curl /health
assertions.actual_result: SIGTERM sent. Log shows 'Shutting down server...' and 'server stopped'. Post-SIGTERM curl fails.
assertions.log_evidence: Shutting down server..., shutting down server, server stopped

assertions.title: In-flight requests drain within shutdown timeout
assertions.command_run: Start loom on port 8095; open SSE; kill -TERM <pid>
assertions.actual_result: Drain completed. Log shows shutdown sequence: 'Shutting down server...', 'server stopped', 'terminal manager stopped'. Server exits after drain.
assertions.log_evidence: Shutdown complete with proper drain sequence
assertions.notes: Server logs 'Warning: server did not shut down within timeout' if drain exceeds deadline, indicating proper drain attempt

assertions.title: SIGINT equivalent to SIGTERM
assertions.actual_result: SIGINT triggered same shutdown sequence. Log shows: 'workspace subscriber stopped', 'health doctor stopped', 'SSE hub stopped', 'multi-pool closed'
assertions.log_evidence: workspace subscriber stopped, multi-workspace subscriber stopped, health doctor stopped, SSE hub stopped, multi-pool closed
assertions.notes: Verified kill -INT produces same graceful shutdown as SIGTERM

assertions.title: Rate-limiter cleanup goroutine stops on shutdown
assertions.actual_result: RateLimiter.Stop() method exists at internal/webui/server/middleware/ratelimit.go:100. It terminates the background cleanup goroutine via close(rl.stopCh). cleanupLoop() runs as goroutine and defers ticker.Stop().
assertions.notes: Verified via code inspection. Stop() closes channel to terminate goroutine.

assertions.title: Second SIGTERM forces exit
assertions.command_run: Start loom on port 8097; send two SIGTERMs ~1s apart
assertions.actual_result: Process exited after double SIGTERM. Log shows shutdown sequence.
assertions.expected_result: Process exits within seconds of second signal

assertions.title: PID file created on daemon start

assertions.expected_result: File exists; contents match running daemon PID
assertions.notes: bd uses .beads/daemon.pid (not ~/.loom/daemon.pid as contract suggests). Also creates .beads/daemon.lock.

assertions.title: PID file removed on clean exit
assertions.actual_result: PID file removed after clean daemon stop

assertions.title: Stale pidfile detected and cleaned on restart
assertions.command_run: Write 999999 to daemon.pid; bd daemon start
assertions.actual_result: Stale PID 999999 replaced with new daemon PID (e.g., 39269). Daemon started successfully.
assertions.expected_result: Daemon starts; pidfile has new PID
assertions.notes: Requires no other daemon running. bd daemon start replaces stale PID.

assertions.title: PID file locked (flock) prevents double-start
assertions.actual_result: Second start rejected with 'Error: daemon already running (PID N, version 0.49.0). Use bd daemon stop to stop it first'
assertions.notes: Uses daemon.lock file with flock for mutual exclusion

assertions.title: Errors only on stderr

assertions.expected_result: Error/warn on stderr only, info on stdout
assertions.notes: Implementation diverges from contract: all structured logs (slog) go to stderr by default. No stdout/stderr split by log level.

assertions.title: Info only on stdout
assertions.actual_result: stdout is empty. All log output (including INFO) goes to stderr via --log-output stderr default.

assertions.title: --log-level flag overrides env var

assertions.notes: --log-level flag is not implemented. Only --log-format and --log-output exist.

assertions.title: Default log level is info

assertions.title: Breaker trips open after N consecutive failures
assertions.actual_result: Breaker stays closed with failure_count=0 even after 20 requests with daemon stopped. Health shows status=degraded but circuit_breaker.state=closed. The pool returns 'daemon unavailable' without incrementing breaker failures.
assertions.notes: The circuit breaker may only track actual connection dial failures, not daemon-unavailable responses. When the pool knows daemon is stopped, it returns errors without attempting a connection, so the breaker is not triggered.

assertions.title: Open breaker fails fast (<50ms)
assertions.actual_result: Requests with daemon unavailable return quickly. avg=3.2ms p99=8.1ms (fast fail without attempting connection).
assertions.notes: Even though breaker doesn't trip to open state, daemon-unavailable fast-fail achieves the same latency goal
